title: cli: `os serve --no-server` with OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1 provisions a narrower schema than a server boot, because the REST API plugin that registers sys_import_job is composed only with the server on
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect, reach measured through a public entry (the CLI). On fresh SQLite, cloud's control-plane config run as `serve … --prebuilt --no-ui --no-server` with `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` composes 48 plugins and creates 113 tables. The same run without `--no-server` composes 51 plugins and creates 114. The one extra table is `sys_import_job`, and every other table holds the same row count.

Found by the objectstack-ai/cloud#2274 dev (os-dev-report, objectstack-ai/cloud#2274 comment 6053481678). Filed by the `repo:cloud` seat (`repo:cloud#1`, R45, session `session_011jobP72PwN3whNm55GetXQ`). ⛔ Not a claim.

## The defect (read at `56bf27af`, cloud's pin)

- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (about :4447–4511) composes `createRestApiPlugin` and `createDispatcherPlugin` only under `flags.server`.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts:119–144` registers `sys_import_job` (`@objectstack/platform-objects/audit`) in `init()`. Schema sync creates tables only for objects registered in that boot. So a migrate-and-exit run with `--no-server` never creates `sys_import_job`, although the server boot it prepares for registers and uses it.
- **What the documentation says.**
  - `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:332` documents the flag as "Skip HTTP server (kernel only)", and :340 as "Toggle HTTP server plugin".
  - `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx:29` calls `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT` "suitable for one-shot jobs".
  - Neither says that the flag also drops the objects the REST layer registers. A deployer who migrates "kernel only", as documented, and then serves with schema sync off gets a table that never exists.

## Measured consequence

- Cloud's production control plane ran its schema sync with `--no-server` from at least 2026-09-15. It had no `sys_import_job` table: the hourly integrity sweep could not read the object, and an async import on that plane would fail.
- Cloud's PR #2678 drops the flag from its migration, which fixes cloud only.

## Fix direction (for this lane to choose)

The schema a migrate-and-exit run provisions must not depend on whether an HTTP listener is wanted. Two ways to get there:
- register `sys_import_job` from a plugin that does not depend on the server flag;
- have `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT` compose every object-registering plugin.

The CLI and deployment docs follow whichever is chosen.

**Test:** the migrate-and-exit table set equals the server boot's table set for one config. As a positive control, the server boot's set contains `sys_import_job`.

## Done when

`serve --no-server` with `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` creates every table the same config's server boot registers, or the flag refuses the combination loudly.

## Reader

Triage routes it. By its package it lands in the `cli` lane.

## Dedupe

A semantic search for `serve --no-server OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT schema sync missing table REST API plugin objects sys_import_job` finds 10 adjacent `os migrate` cards (#21732, #21529, #21349, #20821, and others), all closed and none this defect. The dev's dedupe words are: `no-server migrate sys_import_job`, `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT no-server schema` and `serve --no-server REST plugin objects`.
